case_title: Vaneet Mahajan v. State of Punjab & Ors.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the complainant had instituted four cases against a person (Anil Joshi) at whose alleged instance the attack was carried out. This is the prosecution's allegation, not a court finding.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.307, s.326, s.325, s.324, s.323, s.341, s.427, s.148, s.149 (charges framed by Sessions Judge; FIR also cited s.120-B)
weapon: Swords, daatars (sharp-edged weapons), gandassa, baseball bat, iron rod-type weapons as alleged; sharp-edged weapon caused grievous injuries
evidence_type: Eyewitness (complainant's and witnesses' statements), medical (MLR and injury chart), recovery of weapons and vehicles, call detail records, CCTV footage
aggravating_circumstances: Attack by 10-12 persons armed with swords and other weapons on victims in a car; grievous sharp-edged injuries; victims smashed car glass
trial_court_outcome: Framed charges including s.307 IPC; no trial verdict or sentence stated
high_court_outcome: Revision petition partly allowed; s.307 IPC charge deleted; charges for other offences maintained
neutral_facts: The victim, a practising advocate, was in a car with his brother and an employee when about ten to twelve men attacked it. The assailants were reported to be armed with swords, daatars, a baseball bat and similar weapons. They smashed the front, back and driver's side windows of the car. The victim, seated inside, was struck on the head and bent away, suffering a blow to his right arm. The victim's brother opened the car door to escape, was struck on the head, and suffered finger injuries when he raised his hands to protect himself. He was then chased and injured further. Bystanders gathered after shouting, and the assailants left in their vehicles. The brother drove the injured men to hospital. Medical examination recorded that one injury to each of the two men was grievous and caused by a sharp-edged weapon, with other injuries simple. The employee sustained four simple injuries. During investigation, eleven persons were arrested and the weapons and vehicles used were recovered at their instance. Call detail records and CCTV footage from a nearby bank were analysed. The complainant alleged that the attack was carried out at the instance of a person against whom he had instituted several cases.
physical_harm: Complainant: 11 injuries including two grievous, hospitalised 12 days. Brother: three injuries, one grievous. Employee: four simple injuries. No death.
number_of_offences: 9 charged; 0 finally upheld (s.307 charge restored for trial; no conviction stands)
financial_property_loss: Damage to car windows (front, back and driver's side glass); value not stated
motive: alleged: to teach the complainant a lesson for instituting four cases against a person at whose instance the attack was allegedly carried out
key_evidence_accepted: Complainant's statement and witness statements recorded under s.161 Cr.P.C. in the charge-sheet; medical report showing grievous sharp-edged injuries
witness_credibility: No credibility finding made; Court treated the statements and medical report as supporting the ingredients of s.307 at the framing stage
post_offence_conduct: Alleged in complainant's statement: assailants fled the spot in their cars with weapons after people gathered. Not a court finding.
trial_duration: offence: 10.05.2004 (as stated in para 5; FIR dated 10.05.2014); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 28.08.2015; Supreme Court: 13.04.2017
legal_representation: Appellant (complainant): Manu Sharma, Ms. Ridhima Mandhar, M. Shoeb Alam, Ms. Fauzia Shakil, Ujjwal Singh, Mojahid Karim Khan. Respondents (accused 2-4 and State side): Jitendra Mohan Sharma, Sr. Adv., with Ajit Sharma, Sandeep Singh, Ms. Shweta Jain, Pahlad Singh Sharma. State counsel not separately identified.
investigation_status: FIR registered; SIT investigation; 11 accused arrested; charge-sheet filed; charges framed by Sessions Judge
procedural_irregularity: High Court deleted s.307 charge at the framing stage on the basis that intention was conspicuously missing; Supreme Court held this approach unsustainable
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions Judge): framed charges including s.307. High Court: revision partly allowed, s.307 charge deleted. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, High Court order quashed, accused to be tried under s.307.
prosecution_argument: The complainant/appellant contended the Sessions Judge rightly framed the s.307 IPC charge, and that the attack was intended to kill and was supported by the statements and medical evidence
defence_argument: Accused 2-4 argued medical evidence did not support s.307, intention to kill was conspicuously missing, and at most s.326 applied
legal_principle_applied: Intention or knowledge under s.307 is a question of fact for trial; injury need not be on a fatal part of body; when several persons attack with deadly weapons, knowledge or intention may be presumed; charge stage requires only prima facie ingredients
precedent_relied_upon: Anjani Kumar Chaudhary v. State of Bihar and Another (2014) 12 SCC 286; Vasant Vithu Jadhav v. State of Maharashtra (as quoted in Anjani Kumar)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Several armed assailants attacking unarmed victims with deadly weapons; sharp-edged injuries to head and hands; presumption of intention to kill
other_sentence_order: Accused persons to be tried for offence under s.307 IPC; no compensation or other directions
